toc.title: The shape of a KQL query

html:
1The shape of a KQL query

A Kusto Query Language (KQL) query starts with a table, then passes rows through operators separated by the pipe character.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "-enc"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
Convention Defender XDR tables Sentinel (Log Analytics) tables
Time column Timestamp TimeGenerated
Time filter where Timestamp > ago(1d) where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
Exam tip

. Put the time filter first, then the other filters, then project only the columns you need. Filtering early is the main performance rule.

2Core operators

Operator Purpose
where Filter rows by a predicate
project, project-away, project-rename, project-reorder Select, remove, rename or order columns
extend Add a calculated column
summarize ... by Aggregate (count, dcount, make_set, make_list, arg_max, min, max)
count Number of rows (shorthand for summarize count())
distinct Unique values
take / limit N arbitrary rows (good for testing)
top N by The top N rows by a column
sort by / order by Sort
union Combine tables
join Combine rows of two tables on a key
let Define a variable or a reusable query
parse, mv-expand, make-series, render Parse text, expand arrays, build series, draw a chart
Time and shape functions Meaning
ago(1d) One day before now
bin(Timestamp, 1h) Round a time to a bucket (used with summarize)
*arg_max(Timestamp, ) The latest row per group
make_set(x) Distinct values as an array

3String operators

Operator Behavior
== Exact, case-sensitive
=~ Exact, case-insensitive
has Matches a whole term; fast (uses the term index)
contains Matches any substring; slower
has_any, in Match any of a list
startswith, endswith Prefix or suffix
matches regex Regular expression (slow); prefer parse
!has, !contains, !in Negations

Case-sensitive forms (has_cs, contains_cs, ==) are faster. Terms of three characters or fewer are not indexed.

Exam tip

. has beats contains for speed. =~ and in~ ignore case; == and in do not.

4Joins

The default join flavor is innerunique: it removes duplicate rows from the left side by the join key.

Kind Result
inner Rows with a match on both sides (all matches, no de-duplication)
leftouter All left rows, matches from the right when they exist
leftanti / leftantisemi Left rows with no match on the right (a "not in")
leftsemi Left rows that have a match
fullouter All rows from both sides

Join tips: put the smaller table on the left; filter both sides by time; project only the needed columns before the join; use kind=inner to avoid de-duplication.

5Choosing the table

You need Table
Process creation on devices DeviceProcessEvents
Files created or changed DeviceFileEvents
Network connections from devices DeviceNetworkEvents
Registry changes DeviceRegistryEvents
Logons on devices DeviceLogonEvents
Email delivery and blocking EmailEvents; attachments EmailAttachmentInfo; URLs EmailUrlInfo; clicks UrlClickEvents
On-premises identity IdentityLogonEvents, IdentityQueryEvents, IdentityDirectoryEvents
Cloud app activity CloudAppEvents
Alerts and their evidence AlertInfo, AlertEvidence
Sentinel table Content
SecurityEvent Windows security events
SigninLogs, AuditLogs Entra sign-ins and directory changes
Syslog, CommonSecurityLog Linux logs; CEF logs
AzureActivity Azure subscription operations
OfficeActivity Office 365 activity
SecurityAlert, SecurityIncident Alerts and incidents
Exam tip

. Read the data source in the scenario, then pick the table: process = DeviceProcessEvents, email = EmailEvents, Windows logon = SecurityEvent, Entra sign-in = SigninLogs.

6Three hunting queries

Failed sign-ins per user per hour (Sentinel):

SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) and ResultType != 0
| summarize Failures = count() by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where Failures > 20

Phishing senders (Defender XDR):

EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d) and ThreatTypes has "Phish"
| summarize Mails = count() by SenderFromAddress
| top 10 by Mails desc

Devices that contacted a bad IP, not yet alerted (join):

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d) and RemoteIP in ("203.0.113.5", "198.51.100.7")
| join kind=leftanti (AlertEvidence | where Timestamp > ago(7d)) on DeviceId

7Good habits

Size a new query with count first. Use take to test. Filter early. Avoid unscoped search * and union *; use search in (TableA, TableB). Project only needed columns. Prefer parse over regex. Use ProcessUniqueId instead of PID plus start time to identify a process.

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An analyst filters command lines for the word "invoke" and wants the fastest operator. Which should be used?

  • Acontains, which matches any substring in the text
  • Bmatches regex, which compares a regular expression
  • Chas, which matches a whole term with the index
  • Dstartswith, which matches only the beginning of text
Show the answer

Answer: C. The has operator uses the term index and is faster than contains.

S2A hunter wants to see every process that started on devices in the last day. Which table holds this data?

  • ADeviceFileEvents, with one row per file change
  • BDeviceProcessEvents, with one row per process creation
  • CDeviceLogonEvents, with one row per device sign-in or logon attempt
  • DDeviceNetworkEvents, with one row per connection
Show the answer

Answer: B. DeviceProcessEvents records process creation.

S3Which query returns the number of failed sign-ins per user from SigninLogs?

  • ASigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | summarize count() by UserPrincipalName
  • BSigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | project count() by UserPrincipalName | take 10
  • CSigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | extend count() by UserPrincipalName
  • DSigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | take count() by UserPrincipalName
Show the answer

Answer: A. summarize aggregates rows by a column; project, extend and take do not group.

S4A hunter needs the devices in table A that do not appear in table B. Which join kind fits?

  • Ainner, which keeps only rows with a match on both sides
  • Bleftanti, which keeps left rows that have no match
  • Cfullouter, which keeps all rows from both tables
  • Dleftsemi, which keeps left rows that have a match
Show the answer

Answer: B. leftanti returns the left rows without a match on the right.

S5An analyst wants delivered phishing emails by sender over the past week. Which table should be queried in advanced hunting?

  • AUrlClickEvents, which records clicks on links
  • BCloudAppEvents, which records cloud app activity
  • CIdentityLogonEvents, which records identity sign-in events
  • DEmailEvents, which records email delivery and blocking
Show the answer

Answer: D. EmailEvents holds email delivery data including threat types.

S6A new query on a very large table runs slowly. Which change helps the most?

  • AReplace the time filter with a filter on a calculated column value
  • BUse search * so that every table is checked at the same time
  • CMove the time filter to the beginning and project fewer columns
  • DReplace has with contains to match more text in each row
Show the answer

Answer: C. Filter early on time and other columns, and project only the needed columns.

8.2 Recall questions

R1Which time column do Defender XDR tables use?

Show the answer

Timestamp.

R2Which time column do Sentinel tables use?

Show the answer

TimeGenerated.

R3What is the default join flavor?

Show the answer

innerunique.

R4Which operator rounds times into buckets?

Show the answer

bin.

R5Which table has Windows security events in Sentinel?

Show the answer

SecurityEvent.

R6Which operator is case-insensitive equality?

Show the answer

=~.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Pipeline table
Time Timestamp (Defender), TimeGenerated (Sentinel); ago(); bin()
Strings has fast, contains slow, == case-sensitive, =~ not
Join default innerunique; leftanti for not in; small table on the left
Tables DeviceProcessEvents, EmailEvents, IdentityLogonEvents, SecurityEvent, SigninLogs
Speed filter early, project early, has over contains, no search *
